modal_signal: all fields within it are optional
excerpt: The `ctrdata` register contains metadata for the recorded transfer. This register must be implemented, though all fields within it are optional. Unimplemented fields are read-only 0.

modal_signal: may be writable or may be read-only
excerpt: If bit _i_ of `sie` is read-only zero, the same bit in register `hip` may be writable or may be read-only.

modal_signal: It is optional whether the LCOFI bit (bit 13) in each of mideleg and hideleg ... is implemented and writable
excerpt: It is optional whether the LCOFI bit (bit 13) in each of mideleg and hideleg, which allows all LCOFIs to be delegated to S-mode and VS-mode, respectively, is implemented and writable.

modal_signal: is implementation-defined
excerpt: The size of these naturally aligned power-of-2 regions is implementation-defined, but, for systems with page-based virtual memory, must not exceed the smallest supported page size.

modal_signal: implementations may convert an invalid address into some other invalid address that `sepc` is capable of holding
excerpt: `sepc` is a *WARL* register that must be able to hold all valid virtual addresses. It need not be capable of holding all possible invalid addresses. Prior to writing `sepc`, implementations may convert an invalid address into some other invalid address that `sepc` is capable of holding.

modal_signal: Only if such an extension is implemented will `siselect` be required to support larger values
excerpt: The `siselect` register will support the value range 0..0xFFF at a minimum. A future extension may define a value range outside of this minimum range. Only if such an extension is implemented will `siselect` be required to support larger values.

modal_signal: Only if such an extension is implemented will `vsiselect` be required to support larger values
excerpt: The `vsiselect` register will support the value range 0..0xFFF at a minimum. A future extension may define a value range outside of this minimum range. Only if such an extension is implemented will `vsiselect` be required to support larger values.

modal_signal: Implementations are permitted to resume execution for any reason
excerpt: Implementations are permitted to resume execution for any reason, even if an enabled interrupt has not become pending. Hence, a legal implementation is to simply implement the WFI instruction as a NOP.

modal_signal: platform defined whether the core implementation waits for the bus responses
excerpt: It is platform defined whether the core implementation waits for the bus responses before continuing to the final stage of the sequence, or handles errors responses after completing the PUSH instruction.

modal_signal: may make PPN[1:0] read-only zero
excerpt: An implementation that supports only the defined paged virtual-memory schemes and/or Bare may make PPN[1:0] read-only zero.

modal_signal: is read-only 0 when accessed through sireg*
excerpt: hpmevent__i__ may represent a subset of the state accessed by the mhpmevent__i__ register. Specifically, if Sscofpmf is implemented, event selector bit 62 (MINH) is read-only 0 when accessed through sireg*.

modal_signal: implementations can provide individual read/write bits
excerpt: implementations can provide individual read/write bits within `medeleg` and `mideleg` to indicate that certain exceptions and interrupts should be processed directly by a lower privilege level.

modal_signal: An implementation can choose to subset the delegatable traps
excerpt: An implementation can choose to subset the delegatable traps, with the supported delegatable bits found by writing one to every bit location, then reading back the value in `medeleg` or `mideleg` to see which bit positions hold a one.

modal_signal: an implementation may adopt the stronger model of Total Store Ordering
excerpt: Optionally, an implementation may adopt the stronger model of Total Store Ordering, as defined in <<ztso>>.

modal_signal: the implementation may make FIOM read-only zero
excerpt: If S-mode is not supported, or if `satp`.MODE is read-only zero (always Bare), the implementation may make FIOM read-only zero.

modal_signal: may both be read-only zeros
excerpt: If a system has only one hart, or if a platform standard supports the delivery of machine-level interprocessor interrupts through external interrupts (MEI) instead, then `mip`.MSIP and `mie`.MSIE may both be read-only zeros.

modal_signal: may be read-only zero if there are no extensions implemented that utilize it
excerpt: The `miselect` register implements at least enough bits to support all implemented `miselect` values (corresponding to the implemented extensions that utilize `miselect`/`mireg*` to indirectly access register state). The `miselect` register may be read-only zero if there are no extensions implemented that utilize it.

modal_signal: may implement `mseccfg` such that `[s,u]seed` is a read-only constant value `0`
excerpt: Implementations may implement `mseccfg` such that `[s,u]seed` is a read-only constant value `0`.

modal_signal: Implementations may raise access-fault exceptions instead of address-misaligned exceptions
excerpt: Implementations may raise access-fault exceptions instead of address-misaligned exceptions for some misaligned accesses, indicating the instruction should not be emulated by a trap handler.

modal_signal: Optionally, PMP checks may additionally apply to M-mode accesses
excerpt: Optionally, PMP checks may additionally apply to M-mode accesses, in which case the PMP registers themselves are locked, so that even M-mode software cannot change them until the hart is reset.

modal_signal: may never be 32
excerpt: The bits 1:0 of `ssp` are read-only zero. If the UXLEN or SXLEN may never be 32, then the bit 2 is also read-only zero.

modal_signal: optionally available to U-mode
excerpt: WFI is available in all privileged modes, and optionally available to U-mode.
